A-B Proof of Theorem 1

We first recall the statement of Theorem 1.

Theorem 1.

Let γ\gamma denote the SNR and PP the expected signal power per channel. Let

zr​e​f′=f⁡(xr​e​f′,Θ),zp​o​s′=f⁡(xp​o​s′,Θ),zkn​e​g′=f⁡(xkn​e​g′,Θ)z^{ref^{\prime}}=f(x^{ref^{\prime}};\Theta),\qquad z^{pos^{\prime}}=f(x^{pos^{\prime}};\Theta),\qquad z_{k}^{neg^{\prime}}=f(x_{k}^{neg^{\prime}};\Theta)

denote the noise-perturbed embeddings, and let zr​e​fz^{ref}, zp​o​sz^{pos}, and zkn​e​gz_{k}^{neg} denote their noiseless counterparts. Under the preceding assumptions and lemmas, the following bounds hold, where the expectation is taken over the additive signal noise.

(1) The expected ℓ2\ell_{2}-norm of the gradient of the loss with respect to the layer-ll encoder parameters satisfies

𝔼⁡[‖∇θ¯lℒ​(zr​e​f′,zp​o​s′,{zkn​e​g′}k=1K)‖2]\displaystyle\mathbb{E}\left[\left\|\nabla_{\bar{\theta}_{l}}\mathcal{L}\left(z^{ref^{\prime}},z^{pos^{\prime}},\{z_{k}^{neg^{\prime}}\}_{k=1}^{K}\right)\right\|_{2}\right]
≤‖∇θ¯lℒ​(zr​e​f,zp​o​s,{zkn​e​g}k=1K)‖2+2​(K+2)​Lθ​(l)​G\displaystyle\leq\left\|\nabla_{\bar{\theta}_{l}}\mathcal{L}\left(z^{ref},z^{pos},\{z_{k}^{neg}\}_{k=1}^{K}\right)\right\|_{2}+2(K+2)L_{\theta}(l)G
+Lθ​(l)​Γ​Lx​T​(K+2)3​γ−1​P.\displaystyle\quad+L_{\theta}(l)\Gamma L_{x}\sqrt{T(K+2)^{3}\gamma^{-1}P}. (78)

(2) The corresponding expected squared ℓ2\ell_{2}-norm satisfies

𝔼⁡[‖∇θ¯lℒ​(zr​e​f′,zp​o​s′,{zkn​e​g′}k=1K)‖22]\displaystyle\mathbb{E}\left[\left\|\nabla_{\bar{\theta}_{l}}\mathcal{L}\left(z^{ref^{\prime}},z^{pos^{\prime}},\{z_{k}^{neg^{\prime}}\}_{k=1}^{K}\right)\right\|_{2}^{2}\right]
≤2​‖∇θ¯lℒ​(zr​e​f,zp​o​s,{zkn​e​g}k=1K)‖22+16​(K+2)2​Lθ2​(l)​G2\displaystyle\leq 2\left\|\nabla_{\bar{\theta}_{l}}\mathcal{L}\left(z^{ref},z^{pos},\{z_{k}^{neg}\}_{k=1}^{K}\right)\right\|_{2}^{2}+16(K+2)^{2}L_{\theta}^{2}(l)G^{2}
+4​Lθ2​(l)​Γ2​Lx2​T​(K+2)3​γ−1​P.\displaystyle\quad+4L_{\theta}^{2}(l)\Gamma^{2}L_{x}^{2}T(K+2)^{3}\gamma^{-1}P. (79)

(3) The expected ℓ2\ell_{2}-norm of the gradient with respect to the full encoder parameter vector satisfies

𝔼⁡[‖∇Θℒ​(zr​e​f′,zp​o​s′,{zkn​e​g′}k=1K)‖2]\displaystyle\mathbb{E}\left[\left\|\nabla_{\Theta}\mathcal{L}\left(z^{ref^{\prime}},z^{pos^{\prime}},\{z_{k}^{neg^{\prime}}\}_{k=1}^{K}\right)\right\|_{2}\right]
≤‖∇Θℒ​(zr​e​f,zp​o​s,{zkn​e​g}k=1K)‖2+2​(K+2)​G​∑l=1ΨLθ​(l)\displaystyle\leq\left\|\nabla_{\Theta}\mathcal{L}\left(z^{ref},z^{pos},\{z_{k}^{neg}\}_{k=1}^{K}\right)\right\|_{2}+2(K+2)G\sum_{l=1}^{\Psi}L_{\theta}(l)
+ΓLxT​(K+2)3​γ−1​P∑l=1ΨLθ(l).\displaystyle\quad+\Gamma L_{x}\sqrt{T(K+2)^{3}\gamma^{-1}P}\sum_{l=1}^{\Psi}L_{\theta}(l). (80)

(4) The corresponding expected squared ℓ2\ell_{2}-norm satisfies

𝔼⁡[‖∇Θℒ​(zr​e​f′,zp​o​s′,{zkn​e​g′}k=1K)‖22]\displaystyle\mathbb{E}\left[\left\|\nabla_{\Theta}\mathcal{L}\left(z^{ref^{\prime}},z^{pos^{\prime}},\{z_{k}^{neg^{\prime}}\}_{k=1}^{K}\right)\right\|_{2}^{2}\right]
≤2​‖∇Θℒ​(zr​e​f,zp​o​s,{zkn​e​g}k=1K)‖22+16​(K+2)2​G2​∑l=1ΨLθ2​(l)\displaystyle\leq 2\left\|\nabla_{\Theta}\mathcal{L}\left(z^{ref},z^{pos},\{z_{k}^{neg}\}_{k=1}^{K}\right)\right\|_{2}^{2}+16(K+2)^{2}G^{2}\sum_{l=1}^{\Psi}L_{\theta}^{2}(l)
+4Γ2Lx2T(K+2)3γ−1P∑l=1ΨLθ2(l).\displaystyle\quad+4\Gamma^{2}L_{x}^{2}T(K+2)^{3}\gamma^{-1}P\sum_{l=1}^{\Psi}L_{\theta}^{2}(l). (81)

Here, Lθ​(l)L_{\theta}(l) is the Lipschitz constant of the encoder with respect to its layer-ll parameters, GG bounds the loss gradients with respect to the encoder outputs (Corollary 2), Γ\Gamma is the smoothness constant of the triplet loss (Lemma 4), LxL_{x} is the Lipschitz constant of the encoder with respect to its inputs, TT is the signal length, and Ψ\Psi is the number of encoder layers.

Proof.

For conciseness, define

ℒ′\displaystyle\mathcal{L}^{\prime} ≜ℒ⁡(zr​e​f′,zp​o​s′,{zkn​e​g′}k=1K),\displaystyle\triangleq\mathcal{L}\left(z^{ref^{\prime}},z^{pos^{\prime}},\{z_{k}^{neg^{\prime}}\}_{k=1}^{K}\right), (82)
ℒ\displaystyle\mathcal{L} ≜ℒ⁡(zr​e​f,zp​o​s,{zkn​e​g}k=1K).\displaystyle\triangleq\mathcal{L}\left(z^{ref},z^{pos},\{z_{k}^{neg}\}_{k=1}^{K}\right). (83)

By the chain rule,

∇θ¯lℒ′\displaystyle\nabla_{\bar{\theta}_{l}}\mathcal{L}^{\prime} =Jθ¯l​(xr​e​f′)T​∇zr​e​f′ℒ′+Jθ¯l​(xp​o​s′)T​∇zp​o​s′ℒ′\displaystyle=J_{\bar{\theta}_{l}}(x^{ref^{\prime}})^{T}\nabla_{z^{ref^{\prime}}}\mathcal{L}^{\prime}+J_{\bar{\theta}_{l}}(x^{pos^{\prime}})^{T}\nabla_{z^{pos^{\prime}}}\mathcal{L}^{\prime}
+∑k=1KJθ¯l(xkn​e​g′)T∇zkn​e​g′ℒ′.\displaystyle\quad+\sum_{k=1}^{K}J_{\bar{\theta}_{l}}(x_{k}^{neg^{\prime}})^{T}\nabla_{z_{k}^{neg^{\prime}}}\mathcal{L}^{\prime}. (84)

Similarly,

∇θ¯lℒ\displaystyle\nabla_{\bar{\theta}_{l}}\mathcal{L} =Jθ¯l​(xr​e​f)T​∇zr​e​fℒ+Jθ¯l​(xp​o​s)T​∇zp​o​sℒ\displaystyle=J_{\bar{\theta}_{l}}(x^{ref})^{T}\nabla_{z^{ref}}\mathcal{L}+J_{\bar{\theta}_{l}}(x^{pos})^{T}\nabla_{z^{pos}}\mathcal{L}
+∑k=1KJθ¯l(xkn​e​g)T∇zkn​e​gℒ.\displaystyle\quad+\sum_{k=1}^{K}J_{\bar{\theta}_{l}}(x_{k}^{neg})^{T}\nabla_{z_{k}^{neg}}\mathcal{L}. (85)

Consider first the reference-sample contribution. Adding and subtracting

Jθ¯l​(xr​e​f)T​∇zr​e​f′ℒ′J_{\bar{\theta}_{l}}(x^{ref})^{T}\nabla_{z^{ref^{\prime}}}\mathcal{L}^{\prime}

gives

Jθ¯l​(xr​e​f′)T​∇zr​e​f′ℒ′−Jθ¯l​(xr​e​f)T​∇zr​e​fℒ\displaystyle J_{\bar{\theta}_{l}}(x^{ref^{\prime}})^{T}\nabla_{z^{ref^{\prime}}}\mathcal{L}^{\prime}-J_{\bar{\theta}_{l}}(x^{ref})^{T}\nabla_{z^{ref}}\mathcal{L}
=[Jθ¯l​(xr​e​f′)−Jθ¯l​(xr​e​f)]T​∇zr​e​f′ℒ′\displaystyle=\left[J_{\bar{\theta}_{l}}(x^{ref^{\prime}})-J_{\bar{\theta}_{l}}(x^{ref})\right]^{T}\nabla_{z^{ref^{\prime}}}\mathcal{L}^{\prime}
+Jθ¯l​(xr​e​f)T​[∇zr​e​f′ℒ′−∇zr​e​fℒ].\displaystyle\quad+J_{\bar{\theta}_{l}}(x^{ref})^{T}\left[\nabla_{z^{ref^{\prime}}}\mathcal{L}^{\prime}-\nabla_{z^{ref}}\mathcal{L}\right]. (86)

Therefore,

‖Jθ¯l​(xr​e​f′)T​∇zr​e​f′ℒ′−Jθ¯l​(xr​e​f)T​∇zr​e​fℒ‖2\displaystyle\left\|J_{\bar{\theta}_{l}}(x^{ref^{\prime}})^{T}\nabla_{z^{ref^{\prime}}}\mathcal{L}^{\prime}-J_{\bar{\theta}_{l}}(x^{ref})^{T}\nabla_{z^{ref}}\mathcal{L}\right\|_{2}
≤‖Jθ¯l​(xr​e​f′)−Jθ¯l​(xr​e​f)‖2​‖∇zr​e​f′ℒ′‖2\displaystyle\leq\left\|J_{\bar{\theta}_{l}}(x^{ref^{\prime}})-J_{\bar{\theta}_{l}}(x^{ref})\right\|_{2}\left\|\nabla_{z^{ref^{\prime}}}\mathcal{L}^{\prime}\right\|_{2}
+‖Jθ¯l​(xr​e​f)‖2​‖∇zr​e​f′ℒ′−∇zr​e​fℒ‖2.\displaystyle\quad+\left\|J_{\bar{\theta}_{l}}(x^{ref})\right\|_{2}\left\|\nabla_{z^{ref^{\prime}}}\mathcal{L}^{\prime}-\nabla_{z^{ref}}\mathcal{L}\right\|_{2}. (87)

By Corollaries 1 and 2,

‖Jθ¯l​(xr​e​f′)−Jθ¯l​(xr​e​f)‖2​‖∇zr​e​f′ℒ′‖2≤2​Lθ​(l)​G,\displaystyle\left\|J_{\bar{\theta}_{l}}(x^{ref^{\prime}})-J_{\bar{\theta}_{l}}(x^{ref})\right\|_{2}\left\|\nabla_{z^{ref^{\prime}}}\mathcal{L}^{\prime}\right\|_{2}\leq 2L_{\theta}(l)G, (88)

where we used

‖Jθ¯l​(xr​e​f′)−Jθ¯l​(xr​e​f)‖2≤‖Jθ¯l​(xr​e​f′)‖2+‖Jθ¯l​(xr​e​f)‖2≤2​Lθ​(l).\left\|J_{\bar{\theta}_{l}}(x^{ref^{\prime}})-J_{\bar{\theta}_{l}}(x^{ref})\right\|_{2}\leq\left\|J_{\bar{\theta}_{l}}(x^{ref^{\prime}})\right\|_{2}+\left\|J_{\bar{\theta}_{l}}(x^{ref})\right\|_{2}\leq 2L_{\theta}(l).

By Lemmas 4 and 1,

‖∇zr​e​f′ℒ′−∇zr​e​fℒ‖2\displaystyle\left\|\nabla_{z^{ref^{\prime}}}\mathcal{L}^{\prime}-\nabla_{z^{ref}}\mathcal{L}\right\|_{2}
≤Γ​(‖zr​e​f′−zr​e​f‖22+‖zp​o​s′−zp​o​s‖22+∑k=1K‖zkn​e​g′−zkn​e​g‖22)1/2\displaystyle\leq\Gamma\left(\|z^{ref^{\prime}}-z^{ref}\|_{2}^{2}+\|z^{pos^{\prime}}-z^{pos}\|_{2}^{2}+\sum_{k=1}^{K}\|z_{k}^{neg^{\prime}}-z_{k}^{neg}\|_{2}^{2}\right)^{1/2}
≤Γ​Lx​(‖nr​e​f‖22+‖np​o​s‖22+∑k=1K‖nkn​e​g‖22)1/2.\displaystyle\leq\Gamma L_{x}\left(\|n^{ref}\|_{2}^{2}+\|n^{pos}\|_{2}^{2}+\sum_{k=1}^{K}\|n_{k}^{neg}\|_{2}^{2}\right)^{1/2}. (89)

Since ‖Jθ¯l​(xr​e​f)‖2≤Lθ​(l)\|J_{\bar{\theta}_{l}}(x^{ref})\|_{2}\leq L_{\theta}(l),

‖Jθ¯l​(xr​e​f)‖2​‖∇zr​e​f′ℒ′−∇zr​e​fℒ‖2\displaystyle\left\|J_{\bar{\theta}_{l}}(x^{ref})\right\|_{2}\left\|\nabla_{z^{ref^{\prime}}}\mathcal{L}^{\prime}-\nabla_{z^{ref}}\mathcal{L}\right\|_{2}
≤Lθ​(l)​Γ​Lx​(‖nr​e​f‖22+‖np​o​s‖22+∑k=1K‖nkn​e​g‖22)1/2.\displaystyle\leq L_{\theta}(l)\Gamma L_{x}\left(\|n^{ref}\|_{2}^{2}+\|n^{pos}\|_{2}^{2}+\sum_{k=1}^{K}\|n_{k}^{neg}\|_{2}^{2}\right)^{1/2}. (90)

The same argument applies to the positive sample and to each of the KK negative samples. Hence,

‖∇θ¯lℒ′−∇θ¯lℒ‖2\displaystyle\left\|\nabla_{\bar{\theta}_{l}}\mathcal{L}^{\prime}-\nabla_{\bar{\theta}_{l}}\mathcal{L}\right\|_{2}
≤2​(K+2)​Lθ​(l)​G\displaystyle\leq 2(K+2)L_{\theta}(l)G
+(K+2)​Lθ​(l)​Γ​Lx​(‖nr​e​f‖22+‖np​o​s‖22+∑k=1K‖nkn​e​g‖22)1/2.\displaystyle\quad+(K+2)L_{\theta}(l)\Gamma L_{x}\left(\|n^{ref}\|_{2}^{2}+\|n^{pos}\|_{2}^{2}+\sum_{k=1}^{K}\|n_{k}^{neg}\|_{2}^{2}\right)^{1/2}. (91)

By the reverse triangle inequality,

‖∇θ¯lℒ′‖2≤‖∇θ¯lℒ‖2+‖∇θ¯lℒ′−∇θ¯lℒ‖2.\displaystyle\left\|\nabla_{\bar{\theta}_{l}}\mathcal{L}^{\prime}\right\|_{2}\leq\left\|\nabla_{\bar{\theta}_{l}}\mathcal{L}\right\|_{2}+\left\|\nabla_{\bar{\theta}_{l}}\mathcal{L}^{\prime}-\nabla_{\bar{\theta}_{l}}\mathcal{L}\right\|_{2}. (92)

Combining this inequality with (91) yields

‖∇θ¯lℒ′‖2\displaystyle\left\|\nabla_{\bar{\theta}_{l}}\mathcal{L}^{\prime}\right\|_{2} ≤‖∇θ¯lℒ‖2+2​(K+2)​Lθ​(l)​G\displaystyle\leq\left\|\nabla_{\bar{\theta}_{l}}\mathcal{L}\right\|_{2}+2(K+2)L_{\theta}(l)G
+(K+2)​Lθ​(l)​Γ​Lx​(‖nr​e​f‖22+‖np​o​s‖22+∑k=1K‖nkn​e​g‖22)1/2.\displaystyle\quad+(K+2)L_{\theta}(l)\Gamma L_{x}\left(\|n^{ref}\|_{2}^{2}+\|n^{pos}\|_{2}^{2}+\sum_{k=1}^{K}\|n_{k}^{neg}\|_{2}^{2}\right)^{1/2}. (93)

For independent Gaussian noise with per-coordinate variance γ−1​P\gamma^{-1}P,

𝔼⁡[‖nr​e​f‖22+‖np​o​s‖22+∑k=1K‖nkn​e​g‖22]\displaystyle\mathbb{E}\left[\|n^{ref}\|_{2}^{2}+\|n^{pos}\|_{2}^{2}+\sum_{k=1}^{K}\|n_{k}^{neg}\|_{2}^{2}\right]
=T⁡(K+2)​γ−1​P.\displaystyle=T(K+2)\gamma^{-1}P. (94)

By Jensen’s inequality,

𝔼⁡[(‖nr​e​f‖22+‖np​o​s‖22+∑k=1K‖nkn​e​g‖22)1/2]\displaystyle\mathbb{E}\left[\left(\|n^{ref}\|_{2}^{2}+\|n^{pos}\|_{2}^{2}+\sum_{k=1}^{K}\|n_{k}^{neg}\|_{2}^{2}\right)^{1/2}\right]
≤T⁡(K+2)​γ−1​P.\displaystyle\leq\sqrt{T(K+2)\gamma^{-1}P}. (95)

Taking expectations in (93) therefore gives

𝔼⁡[‖∇θ¯lℒ′‖2]\displaystyle\mathbb{E}\left[\left\|\nabla_{\bar{\theta}_{l}}\mathcal{L}^{\prime}\right\|_{2}\right]
≤‖∇θ¯lℒ‖2+2​(K+2)​Lθ​(l)​G\displaystyle\leq\left\|\nabla_{\bar{\theta}_{l}}\mathcal{L}\right\|_{2}+2(K+2)L_{\theta}(l)G
+Lθ​(l)​Γ​Lx​T​(K+2)3​γ−1​P,\displaystyle\quad+L_{\theta}(l)\Gamma L_{x}\sqrt{T(K+2)^{3}\gamma^{-1}P}, (96)

which proves statement (1).

To prove statement (2), let

dl≜∇θ¯lℒ′−∇θ¯lℒ.d_{l}\triangleq\nabla_{\bar{\theta}_{l}}\mathcal{L}^{\prime}-\nabla_{\bar{\theta}_{l}}\mathcal{L}.

From (91) and (a+b)2≤2​a2+2​b2(a+b)^{2}\leq 2a^{2}+2b^{2},

‖dl‖22\displaystyle\|d_{l}\|_{2}^{2} ≤8​(K+2)2​Lθ2​(l)​G2\displaystyle\leq 8(K+2)^{2}L_{\theta}^{2}(l)G^{2}
+2​(K+2)2​Lθ2​(l)​Γ2​Lx2​(‖nr​e​f‖22+‖np​o​s‖22+∑k=1K‖nkn​e​g‖22).\displaystyle\quad+2(K+2)^{2}L_{\theta}^{2}(l)\Gamma^{2}L_{x}^{2}\left(\|n^{ref}\|_{2}^{2}+\|n^{pos}\|_{2}^{2}+\sum_{k=1}^{K}\|n_{k}^{neg}\|_{2}^{2}\right). (97)

Moreover,

‖∇θ¯lℒ′‖22\displaystyle\left\|\nabla_{\bar{\theta}_{l}}\mathcal{L}^{\prime}\right\|_{2}^{2} =‖∇θ¯lℒ+dl‖22\displaystyle=\left\|\nabla_{\bar{\theta}_{l}}\mathcal{L}+d_{l}\right\|_{2}^{2}
≤2​‖∇θ¯lℒ‖22+2​‖dl‖22.\displaystyle\leq 2\left\|\nabla_{\bar{\theta}_{l}}\mathcal{L}\right\|_{2}^{2}+2\|d_{l}\|_{2}^{2}. (98)

Taking expectations yields

𝔼⁡[‖∇θ¯lℒ′‖22]\displaystyle\mathbb{E}\left[\left\|\nabla_{\bar{\theta}_{l}}\mathcal{L}^{\prime}\right\|_{2}^{2}\right]
≤2​‖∇θ¯lℒ‖22+16​(K+2)2​Lθ2​(l)​G2\displaystyle\leq 2\left\|\nabla_{\bar{\theta}_{l}}\mathcal{L}\right\|_{2}^{2}+16(K+2)^{2}L_{\theta}^{2}(l)G^{2}
+4​Lθ2​(l)​Γ2​Lx2​T​(K+2)3​γ−1​P,\displaystyle\quad+4L_{\theta}^{2}(l)\Gamma^{2}L_{x}^{2}T(K+2)^{3}\gamma^{-1}P, (99)

which proves statement (2).

For the full encoder parameter vector,

∇Θℒ′=[∇θ¯1ℒ′∇θ¯Ψℒ′],∇Θℒ=[∇θ¯1ℒ∇θ¯Ψℒ].\nabla_{\Theta}\mathcal{L}^{\prime}=\begin{bmatrix}\nabla_{\bar{\theta}_{1}}\mathcal{L}^{\prime}\\ \vdots\\ \nabla_{\bar{\theta}_{\Psi}}\mathcal{L}^{\prime}\end{bmatrix},\qquad\nabla_{\Theta}\mathcal{L}=\begin{bmatrix}\nabla_{\bar{\theta}_{1}}\mathcal{L}\\ \vdots\\ \nabla_{\bar{\theta}_{\Psi}}\mathcal{L}\end{bmatrix}.

Using

‖∇Θℒ′−∇Θℒ‖2≤∑l=1Ψ‖dl‖2\left\|\nabla_{\Theta}\mathcal{L}^{\prime}-\nabla_{\Theta}\mathcal{L}\right\|_{2}\leq\sum_{l=1}^{\Psi}\|d_{l}\|_{2}

together with (91), we obtain

‖∇Θℒ′‖2\displaystyle\left\|\nabla_{\Theta}\mathcal{L}^{\prime}\right\|_{2}
≤‖∇Θℒ‖2+2​(K+2)​G​∑l=1ΨLθ​(l)\displaystyle\leq\left\|\nabla_{\Theta}\mathcal{L}\right\|_{2}+2(K+2)G\sum_{l=1}^{\Psi}L_{\theta}(l)
+(K+2)​Γ​Lx​(∑l=1ΨLθ​(l))​(‖nr​e​f‖22+‖np​o​s‖22+∑k=1K‖nkn​e​g‖22)1/2.\displaystyle\quad+(K+2)\Gamma L_{x}\left(\sum_{l=1}^{\Psi}L_{\theta}(l)\right)\left(\|n^{ref}\|_{2}^{2}+\|n^{pos}\|_{2}^{2}+\sum_{k=1}^{K}\|n_{k}^{neg}\|_{2}^{2}\right)^{1/2}. (100)

Taking expectations proves statement (3).

Finally, since

‖∇Θℒ′‖22=∑l=1Ψ‖∇θ¯lℒ′‖22,\left\|\nabla_{\Theta}\mathcal{L}^{\prime}\right\|_{2}^{2}=\sum_{l=1}^{\Psi}\left\|\nabla_{\bar{\theta}_{l}}\mathcal{L}^{\prime}\right\|_{2}^{2},

summing the layerwise bounds from statement (2) gives

𝔼⁡[‖∇Θℒ′‖22]\displaystyle\mathbb{E}\left[\left\|\nabla_{\Theta}\mathcal{L}^{\prime}\right\|_{2}^{2}\right]
≤2​‖∇Θℒ‖22+16​(K+2)2​G2​∑l=1ΨLθ2​(l)\displaystyle\leq 2\left\|\nabla_{\Theta}\mathcal{L}\right\|_{2}^{2}+16(K+2)^{2}G^{2}\sum_{l=1}^{\Psi}L_{\theta}^{2}(l)
+4Γ2Lx2T(K+2)3γ−1P∑l=1ΨLθ2(l),\displaystyle\quad+4\Gamma^{2}L_{x}^{2}T(K+2)^{3}\gamma^{-1}P\sum_{l=1}^{\Psi}L_{\theta}^{2}(l), (101)

which proves statement (4). ∎

A-C Proof of Theorem 2

Theorem 2.

Assume that the local losses are BdissB_{\text{diss}}-locally dissimilar at Θt\Theta^{t} , and that

Bdiss​ηie<1.B_{\mathrm{diss}}\eta_{\mathrm{ie}}<1.

Then for any SNR γ\gamma, signal power PP, and heterogeneous client data distributions, we can choose μprox>L−\mu_{\text{prox}}>L_{-} large enough such that

ℒglobal​(Θt+1)\displaystyle\mathcal{L}_{\text{global}}(\Theta^{t+1}) ≤ℒglobal​(Θt)−𝒪⁡(1μprox)​‖∇ℒglobal​(Θt)‖22\displaystyle\leq\mathcal{L}_{\text{global}}(\Theta^{t})-\mathcal{O}\left(\frac{1}{\mu_{\text{prox}}}\right)\|\nabla\mathcal{L}_{\text{global}}(\Theta^{t})\|^{2}_{2} (102)
+𝒪(1μprox)⋅Err(γ,P,Bdiss,ηie,Θt),\displaystyle\quad+\mathcal{O}\left(\frac{1}{\mu_{\text{prox}}}\right)\cdot\mathrm{Err}(\gamma,P,B_{\text{diss}},\eta_{\text{ie}},\Theta^{t}), (103)

where the variance term captures the impact of signal noise, client heterogeneity, and inexact updates.

Proof:

We begin by recalling important results from our proofs presented for Theorem 1 which we will use to prove this theorem. From our definitions

ℒc​(Θ)=𝔼x∼𝒟c,n​[ℒ⁡(Θ,x+n)].\displaystyle\mathcal{L}_{c}(\Theta)=\mathbb{E}_{x\sim\mathcal{D}_{c},\,n}\big[\mathcal{L}(\Theta;x+n)\big]. (104)

and

ℒcclean​(Θ)=𝔼x∼𝒟c​[ℒ⁡(Θ,x)],\displaystyle\mathcal{L}_{c}^{\mathrm{clean}}(\Theta)=\mathbb{E}_{x\sim\mathcal{D}_{c}}\big[\mathcal{L}(\Theta;x)\big], (105)

and applying Jensen’s inequality, we have

‖∇ℒc​(Θt)−∇ℒcc​l​e​a​n​(Θt)‖2\displaystyle||\nabla\mathcal{L}_{c}(\Theta^{t})-\nabla\mathcal{L}^{clean}_{c}(\Theta^{t})||_{2} ≤𝔼x∼𝒟c​[‖𝔼n|x​[∇ℒ​(Θt,x+n)−∇ℒ​(Θt,x)]‖2].\displaystyle\leq\mathbb{E}_{x\sim\mathcal{D}_{c}}\big[||\mathbb{E}_{n|x}\big[\nabla\mathcal{L}(\Theta^{t};x+n)-\nabla\mathcal{L}(\Theta^{t};x)\big]||_{2}\big].
≤𝔼x∼𝒟c​[𝔼n|x​[‖∇ℒ​(Θt,x+n)−∇ℒ​(Θt,x)‖2]]\displaystyle\leq\mathbb{E}_{x\sim\mathcal{D}_{c}}\big[\mathbb{E}_{n|x}\big[||\nabla\mathcal{L}(\Theta^{t};x+n)-\nabla\mathcal{L}(\Theta^{t};x)||_{2}\big]\big]
=𝔼x∼𝒟c​[𝔼n​[‖∇ℒ​(Θt,x+n)−∇ℒ​(Θt,x)‖2]]\displaystyle=\mathbb{E}_{x\sim\mathcal{D}_{c}}\big[\mathbb{E}_{n}\big[||\nabla\mathcal{L}(\Theta^{t};x+n)-\nabla\mathcal{L}(\Theta^{t};x)||_{2}\big]\big]
≤𝔼x∼𝒟c[2(K+2)G∑l=1ΨLθ(l)\displaystyle\leq\mathbb{E}_{x\sim\mathcal{D}_{c}}\big[2(K+2)G\sum_{l=1}^{\Psi}L_{\theta}(l)
+ΓLxT​(K+2)3​γ−1​P∑l=1ΨLθ(l).]\displaystyle\quad+\Gamma L_{x}\sqrt{T(K+2)^{3}\gamma^{-1}P}\sum_{l=1}^{\Psi}L_{\theta}(l).\big]
=2​(K+2)​G​∑l=1ΨLθ​(l)+Γ​Lx​T​(K+2)3​γ−1​P​∑l=1ΨLθ​(l)\displaystyle=2(K+2)G\sum_{l=1}^{\Psi}L_{\theta}(l)+\Gamma L_{x}\sqrt{T(K+2)^{3}\gamma^{-1}P}\sum_{l=1}^{\Psi}L_{\theta}(l)

where we use the fact that the noise is independent of signal. We now proceed to the main proof.

Introducing μ¯p​r​o​x=μp​r​o​x−L−\bar{\mu}_{prox}=\mu_{prox}-L_{-}, we seek to prove

ℒg​l​o​b​a​l​(Θt+1)\displaystyle\mathcal{L}_{global}({\Theta}^{t+1})
≤ℒg​l​o​b​a​l​(Θt)−(1μp​r​o​x−Bd​i​s​s​ηi​eμp​r​o​x−Bd​i​s​s​Ll​o​s​sa​l​l​(1+ηi​e)μp​r​o​x​μ¯p​r​o​x−3​Bd​i​s​s2​Ll​o​s​sa​l​l​(1+ηi​e)22​μ¯p​r​o​x2)​‖∇ℒg​l​o​b​a​l​(Θt)‖22\displaystyle\leq\mathcal{L}_{global}(\Theta^{t})-\bigg(\frac{1}{\mu_{prox}}-\frac{B_{diss}\eta_{ie}}{\mu_{prox}}-\frac{B_{diss}L^{all}_{loss}(1+\eta_{ie})}{\mu_{prox}\bar{\mu}_{prox}}-\frac{3B_{diss}^{2}L^{all}_{loss}(1+\eta_{ie})^{2}}{2\bar{\mu}^{2}_{prox}}\bigg)||\nabla\mathcal{L}_{global}(\Theta^{t})||^{2}_{2}
+(2​(K+2)​G​(Ll​o​s​sa​l​l​(1+ηi​e)μp​r​o​x​μ¯p​r​o​x)​∑l=1ΨLθ​(l)+Γ​Lx​T​(K+2)3​γ−1​P​(Ll​o​s​sa​l​l​(1+ηi​e)μp​r​o​x​μ¯p​r​o​x)​∑l=1ΨLθ​(l))​‖∇ℒg​l​o​b​a​l​(Θt)‖2\displaystyle+\bigg(2(K+2)G\bigg(\frac{L^{all}_{loss}(1+\eta_{ie})}{\mu_{prox}\bar{\mu}_{prox}}\bigg)\sum_{l=1}^{\Psi}L_{\theta}(l)+\Gamma L_{x}\sqrt{T(K+2)^{3}\gamma^{-1}P}\bigg(\frac{L^{all}_{loss}(1+\eta_{ie})}{\mu_{prox}\bar{\mu}_{prox}}\bigg)\sum_{l=1}^{\Psi}L_{\theta}(l)\bigg)||\nabla\mathcal{L}_{global}(\Theta^{t})||_{2}
+(12​(K+2)2​G2​Ll​o​s​sa​l​l​(1+ηi​e)2μ¯p​r​o​x2​(∑l=1ΨLθ​(l))2+3​Γ2​Lx2​T​(K+2)3​γ−1​P​(1+ηi​e)22​μ¯p​r​o​x2​(∑l=1ΨLθ​(l))2)+\displaystyle+\bigg(\frac{12(K+2)^{2}G^{2}L^{all}_{loss}(1+\eta_{ie})^{2}}{\bar{\mu}_{prox}^{2}}(\sum_{l=1}^{\Psi}L_{\theta}(l))^{2}+\frac{3\Gamma^{2}L_{x}^{2}T(K+2)^{3}\gamma^{-1}P(1+\eta_{ie})^{2}}{2\bar{\mu}_{prox}^{2}}(\sum_{l=1}^{\Psi}L_{\theta}(l))^{2}\bigg)+
(2​(K+2)​G​(1+ηi​eμp​r​o​x)​∑l=1ΨLθ​(l)+Γ​Lx​T​(K+2)3​γ−1​P​(1+ηi​eμp​r​o​x)​∑l=1ΨLθ​(l))​‖∇ℒg​l​o​b​a​l​(Θt)‖2\displaystyle\bigg(2(K+2)G\bigg(\frac{1+\eta_{ie}}{\mu_{prox}}\bigg)\sum_{l=1}^{\Psi}L_{\theta}(l)+\Gamma L_{x}\sqrt{T(K+2)^{3}\gamma^{-1}P}\bigg(\frac{1+\eta_{ie}}{\mu_{prox}}\bigg)\sum_{l=1}^{\Psi}L_{\theta}(l)\bigg)||\nabla\mathcal{L}_{global}(\Theta^{t})||_{2} (106)

Let us define

ect+1=∇ℒc​(Θct+1)+μp​r​o​x​(Θct+1−Θt).\displaystyle\color[rgb]{0,0,0}e_{c}^{t+1}=\nabla\mathcal{L}_{c}(\Theta_{c}^{t+1})+\mu_{prox}(\Theta_{c}^{t+1}-\Theta^{t}). (107)

By definition of inexactness and Assumption 6, we obtain

‖ect+1‖≤ηi​e​‖∇ℒc​(Θt)‖\displaystyle||e_{c}^{t+1}||\leq\eta_{ie}||\nabla\mathcal{L}_{c}(\Theta^{t})|| (108)

Taking expectation, we get

Θ¯t+1=𝔼c​[Θct+1]\displaystyle\bar{\Theta}^{t+1}=\mathbb{E}_{c}[\Theta_{c}^{t+1}] (109)

which yields

Θ¯t+1−Θt=−1μp​r​o​x​𝔼c​[∇ℒc​(Θct+1)]+1μp​r​o​x​𝔼c​[ect+1]\displaystyle\bar{\Theta}^{t+1}-\Theta^{t}=-\frac{1}{\mu_{prox}}\mathbb{E}_{c}[\nabla\mathcal{L}_{c}(\Theta_{c}^{t+1})]+\frac{1}{\mu_{prox}}\mathbb{E}_{c}[e_{c}^{t+1}] (110)

Recall that we have defined μ¯p​r​o​x=μp​r​o​x−L−\bar{\mu}_{prox}=\mu_{prox}-L_{-}. By the optimality condition

∇hc​(Θ^ct+1,Θt)=0\displaystyle\color[rgb]{0,0,0}\nabla h_{c}(\hat{\Theta}_{c}^{t+1},\Theta^{t})=0 (111)

and by μ¯p​r​o​x\bar{\mu}_{prox}-strong convexity of hc​()h_{c}(), for any Θ\Theta

hc​(Θ,Θt)≥hc​(Θ^ct+1,Θt)+μ¯p​r​o​x2​‖Θ−Θ^ct+1‖22\displaystyle\color[rgb]{0,0,0}h_{c}(\Theta,\Theta^{t})\geq h_{c}(\hat{\Theta}_{c}^{t+1},\Theta^{t})+\frac{\bar{\mu}_{prox}}{2}||\Theta-\hat{\Theta}_{c}^{t+1}||_{2}^{2} (112)

Strong convexity also implies

≤Lθ​(l)​Γ​Lx​(‖nr​e​f‖22+‖np​o​s‖22+∑k=1K‖nkn​e​g‖22)1/2.\displaystyle\leq L_{\theta}(l)\Gamma L_{x}\left(\|n^{ref}\|_{2}^{2}+\|n^{pos}\|_{2}^{2}+\sum_{k=1}^{K}\|n_{k}^{neg}\|_{2}^{2}\right)^{1/2}. (130)

Applying the same argument to the positive sample and all KK negative samples yields

‖∇θ¯lℒ′−∇θ¯lℒ‖2\displaystyle\left\|\nabla_{\bar{\theta}_{l}}\mathcal{L}^{\prime}-\nabla_{\bar{\theta}_{l}}\mathcal{L}\right\|_{2}

+(K+2)​Lθ​(l)​Γ​Lx​(‖nr​e​f‖22+‖np​o​s‖22+∑k=1K‖nkn​e​g‖22)1/2.\displaystyle\quad+(K+2)L_{\theta}(l)\Gamma L_{x}\left(\|n^{ref}\|_{2}^{2}+\|n^{pos}\|_{2}^{2}+\sum_{k=1}^{K}\|n_{k}^{neg}\|_{2}^{2}\right)^{1/2}. (131)

For independent Gaussian noise with per-coordinate variance γ−1​P\gamma^{-1}P,

𝔼​‖n‖2≤𝔼​‖n‖22=T​γ−1​P,\mathbb{E}\|n\|_{2}\leq\sqrt{\mathbb{E}\|n\|_{2}^{2}}=\sqrt{T\gamma^{-1}P},

and

𝔼⁡[‖nr​e​f‖22+‖np​o​s‖22+∑k=1K‖nkn​e​g‖22]=T⁡(K+2)​γ−1​P.\mathbb{E}\left[\|n^{ref}\|_{2}^{2}+\|n^{pos}\|_{2}^{2}+\sum_{k=1}^{K}\|n_{k}^{neg}\|_{2}^{2}\right]=T(K+2)\gamma^{-1}P.

Taking expectations in (131) and applying the reverse triangle inequality proves the first bound.

For the squared-gradient bound, let

dl=∇θ¯lℒ′−∇θ¯lℒ.d_{l}=\nabla_{\bar{\theta}_{l}}\mathcal{L}^{\prime}-\nabla_{\bar{\theta}_{l}}\mathcal{L}.

By Cauchy–Schwarz,

(‖nr​e​f‖2+‖np​o​s‖2+∑k=1K‖nkn​e​g‖2)2≤(K+2)​(‖nr​e​f‖22+‖np​o​s‖22+∑k=1K‖nkn​e​g‖22).\left(\|n^{ref}\|_{2}+\|n^{pos}\|_{2}+\sum_{k=1}^{K}\|n_{k}^{neg}\|_{2}\right)^{2}\leq(K+2)\left(\|n^{ref}\|_{2}^{2}+\|n^{pos}\|_{2}^{2}+\sum_{k=1}^{K}\|n_{k}^{neg}\|_{2}^{2}\right).

Using (a+b)2≤2​a2+2​b2(a+b)^{2}\leq 2a^{2}+2b^{2} in (131), followed by

‖∇θ¯lℒ′‖22≤2​‖∇θ¯lℒ‖22+2​‖dl‖22,\|\nabla_{\bar{\theta}_{l}}\mathcal{L}^{\prime}\|_{2}^{2}\leq 2\|\nabla_{\bar{\theta}_{l}}\mathcal{L}\|_{2}^{2}+2\|d_{l}\|_{2}^{2},

gives the second bound after taking expectations.

The full-parameter gradient is obtained by stacking the layerwise gradients. Summing the first-order layerwise estimates gives the third bound, while summing the corrected squared layerwise estimates gives the fourth bound. ∎

Appendix B Miscellaneous

B-A Mobility-induced carrier frequency offset

This subsection provides a simplified relation between carrier frequency offset (CFO) and relative motion between a transmitter and receiver. Such mobility-induced offsets may vary across clients and thereby introduce heterogeneity into federated representation learning.

Let fcf_{c} denote the nominal carrier frequency to which the receiver’s local oscillator is tuned, and let νr\nu_{r} denote the radial velocity of the transmitter relative to the receiver. Under the classical Doppler model for a moving transmitter and stationary receiver, the observed carrier frequency is

fo=fc​(1∓νrc)−1,\displaystyle f_{o}=f_{c}\left(1\mp\frac{\nu_{r}}{c}\right)^{-1}, (134)

where cc is the speed of light. The minus sign corresponds to motion toward the receiver and the plus sign to motion away from it. For νr≪c\nu_{r}\ll c, a first-order approximation gives

fo≈fc​(1±νrc),\displaystyle f_{o}\approx f_{c}\left(1\pm\frac{\nu_{r}}{c}\right), (135)

where the positive sign corresponds to an approaching transmitter.

Consider the approaching case, for which the Doppler shift is positive. The received passband signal can be represented as

A~​(t)​cos⁡(2​π​fo​t+θ~​(t)),\tilde{A}(t)\cos\left(2\pi f_{o}t+\tilde{\theta}(t)\right),

where A~​(t)\tilde{A}(t) and θ~​(t)\tilde{\theta}(t) represent the amplitude and phase modulation, respectively. After downconversion using a local oscillator at frequency fcf_{c} and sampling at rate fsf_{s}, the corresponding complex baseband signal is

r⁡[n]=A~​[n]​ej​(2​π​fc​νrfs​c​n+θ~​[n])+w⁡[n],\displaystyle r[n]=\tilde{A}[n]e^{j\left(2\pi\frac{f_{c}\nu_{r}}{f_{s}c}n+\tilde{\theta}[n]\right)}+w[n], (136)

where w⁡[n]w[n] denotes complex baseband noise. The resulting normalized CFO is therefore

Δ​f=fc​νrfs​c.\displaystyle\Delta f=\frac{f_{c}\nu_{r}}{f_{s}c}. (137)

This offset produces a phase rotation that accumulates linearly with the sample index. Consequently, differences in carrier frequency, sampling rate, and radial velocity across clients can produce different values of Δ​f\Delta f, introducing client heterogeneity during federated encoder training.

B-B Effect of varying α¯\bar{\alpha} on label distributions

Figures 8 and 9 show the client-wise label distributions obtained by Dirichlet partitioning of the MIGOU dataset across four clients for different values of α¯\bar{\alpha}. Smaller values of α¯\bar{\alpha} produce more highly skewed client distributions, whereas larger values yield increasingly uniform partitions.
